The main takeaway from our work is that
bone mineral density (and bone strength) is lower in postmenopausal women compared to premenopausal women.
the menopause is associated with increased bone turnover and bone loss in the femoral neck and Ward's triangle but not in the trochanter.
bone loss in the hip begins in the fourth decade of life, and the rate of loss is accelerated by the menopause, with a mean loss of 3% per year in the first 5 years after the menopause.
